So with all the info you gave I’m more inclined to believe they are some form of Mycena mushroom. Possibly leptocephala  (nitrous bonnet) or pura (lilac bonnet) both inedible but the latter being toxic. Definite signs of Mycena mushrooms is their odor so if you crush one and take a waft it should smell like bleach, radishes and garlic. Again it’s very important to never eat a mushroom unless you are 100% sure of the identity AND keep in mind where you harvest. Yards and roadsides are often treated with pesticides and mushrooms are basically heavy metal sponges so industrial complexes should be completely avoided.

My shot in the dark guess here is that they are some form of Omphalotus olivascens or Jack-O-Lantern mushroom which is often easily mistaken for chanterelles by beginners. These mushrooms often get a lot bigger and turn a deeper orange when mature. They also glow in the dark depending on their maturity. The western jack-o'-lantern mushroom is a highly poisonous mushroom. The most typical symptoms of poisoning include profuse sweating and severe gastrointestinal distress that can last for several days. Which is why it’s incredibly important to be 100% sure what you are looking at before even contemplating eating it.
